plot_series — ANNOTATE plot op

• Data kinds: image2d × axes × signal × signal → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.plot_series(img, axes, x, y, kind='line', color='reference', width=2, marker_size=3, baseline=None, bar_width=0.7, clip=True, scheme='okabe_ito', style=None) (to call the implementation directly, import annotate; annotate.plot_series(img, axes, x, y, kind='line', color='reference', width=2, marker_size=3, baseline=None, bar_width=0.7, clip=True, scheme='okabe_ito', style=None); from the registry, opsannotate.get("plot_series"))

Usage

Draw lines, scatter or bars. Takes data coordinates (the axes decide the pixels).

Parameters

axes : dict

The return of axes_transform.

x, y : 1-D

Series of the same length. Empty is a ValueError (with an empty graph you cannot tell "there is no data"

from "forgot to draw").

kind : {'line','scatter','bar'}

baseline : float or None

Reference value for kind='bar'. If None, the lower end of ylim.

bar_width : float

Bar width (ratio to the spacing between neighbouring x, ∈ (0,1]).

clip : bool

If True, points that leave the drawing area are an exception (the clamping in imagedraw,

which silently sticks them to the edge, would draw a lying polyline).

Raises

ValueError

length mismatch / empty / non-finite / unknown kind / out of range with clip=True.
